title: Kubelet startup race condition - quickdebug scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
Short scratchpad capturing commands I ran during the cluster/node provisioning incident where kubelet failed intermittently at boot (nodes flapped NotReady for ~2-5 mins). Hoping this saves time next rotation and surfaces a reproducible pattern.

Timeline notes (observed behavior):
- New GKE node boots, cloud-init applies kubelet config, kubelet.service starts, CRI (containerd) starts.
- Node intermittently reports NotReady for ~1-4 minutes; kubelet logs show errors: failed to create pod sandbox / cni plugin errors / volume attach timeouts.
- Problem seems correlated with heavy ephemeral disk attach activity (many PVCs mounting on node) and node-provision bootstrap ordering.

Key hypotheses (ordered by likelihood):
1) Race between kubelet starting and volume/disk/udev devices being available -> kubelet gives up on mounts, marks node NotReady.
2) CNI plugin (multus or calico) not ready because network config generated by init script runs after kubelet.
3) systemd service ordering/Requires not strict enough in our cloud-init; kubelet lacks dependency on local-fs-pre or cloud-config signal.
4) Transient credential fetch (KMS) for Kubelet TLS causing temporary 401s -> kubelet moves to NotReady until certs present. Less likely but saw one token-refresh error in logs.

Commands I ran (useful for reproducing / collecting more logs):
- Check node health quickly:
  kubectl get nodes -o wide | egrep "NotReady|Ready"

- Watch kubelet journald live on a repro node (SSH):
  sudo journalctl -u kubelet -f --no-hostname --output=cat
  # look for: "failed to start containerd" or "error getting node status"

- Grep for mount / volume errors:
  sudo journalctl -u kubelet |& egrep -i "mount|attach|volume|pv|pvc|failed to mount|device busy|timeout" | tail -n 200

- Inspect systemd ordering and cloud-init steps that touch /var/lib/kubelet:
  systemctl show -p After kubelet.service
  systemctl status cloud-final.service cloud-init.service
  ls -l /var/lib/kubelet /var/lib/kubelet/pods | head -n 30

- Container runtime status:
  sudo systemctl status containerd
  sudo crictl ps --runtime-endpoint unix:///run/containerd/containerd.sock
  sudo crictl info --runtime-endpoint unix:///run/containerd/containerd.sock

- CNI troubleshooting (on node):
  ls -la /etc/cni/net.d/
  cat /etc/cni/net.d/* | sed -n '1,200p'
  sudo ls -l /opt/cni/bin/

- Quick check for missing kernel modules / udev:
  sudo udevadm settle --timeout=10
  dmesg | tail -n 80

- Check for disk attach timing (if using CSI driver):
  sudo journalctl -u csi-attacher -f --no-hostname
  kubectl -n kube-system logs deployment/csi-driver -c attacher --tail=200

- Debug volume mounts from kubelet POV (search log examples):
  # example failure: "MountVolume.WaitForAttach failed for volume \"pvc-xxx\" : device not found"

Interesting log snippets I captured (redacted):
- Oct 18 09:22:10 host-123 kubelet[1234]: E1018 09:22:10.234567 1234 nestedpendingoperations.go:301] Operation for "volumeName" failed. No retries left.
- Oct 18 09:22:11 host-123 kubelet[1234]: W1018 09:22:11.345678 1234 kubelet_volumes.go:217] MountVolume.WaitForAttach failed for volume "pvc-xxx": device not found
- Oct 18 09:22:13 host-123 containerd[995]: time="2024-10-18T09:22:13.123Z" level=error msg="failed to create shim task"...
- Oct 18 09:22:15 host-123 cloud-init[789]: Running script: configure-local-disks.sh -> created /dev/disk/by-id/ nvme* mapping
- Oct 18 09:22:18 host-123 kubelet[1234]: E1018 09:22:18.456789 1234 cni.go:362] CNI failed to set up pod "nginx-xx" network: error adding network: failed to open netns file "/proc/xxx/ns/net": no such file or directory

What I changed / experiments: (results noted)
A) Force kubelet to wait for /var/lib/cloud/instance/boot-finished marker (w/ systemd drop-in):
  /etc/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/10-wait-for-cloud.conf
  [Unit]
  After=cloud-final.service
  Wants=cloud-final.service
  # RESULT: Reduced NotReady frequency from ~30% boots to ~8%. Suggests ordering issue.

B) Added udevadm settle call in pre-script before starting kubelet (cloud-init oneshot).
  # RESULT: Some improvement but not fully eliminated; still saw mount timeouts when many PVCs attached concurrently.

C) Tweak kubelet flags to increase mount timeout / enable mount propagation debugging:
  --volume-plugin-dir=/var/lib/kubelet/volumeplugins --enable-controller-attach-detach=true --pod-manifest-path=/etc/kubernetes/manifests
  # RESULT: No immediate improvement; mount errors persisted during high attach bursts.

D) Temporarily serialised CSI attach operations by limiting concurrent attach goroutines in CSI controller (test cluster change).
  # RESULT: Eliminated failures in controlled run, but this is a bandaid (reduces throughput).

Notes on Helm / cluster provisioning hooks (because some clusters use helm charts with initJobs):
- We have a helm chart that creates an initJob to pre-provision disks on nodes (via DaemonSet + hostPath in chart). If initJob runs after kubelet is up it can be fine; if the job writes /dev links late, kubelet may race.
- When using helm hooks and InitContainers that touch host devices, ensure hook weight and kubelet start ordering are compatible.

Repro recipe (manual):
1) Create a node pool that boots with user-data that intentionally delays /dev population by 20s (simulate flaky storage attach).
2) Boot 5 nodes concurrently, observe kubelet/journal logs for first ~120s.
3) Inspect which boot ordering (cloud-init -> containerd -> kubelet) differs across nodes that become Ready vs NotReady.

Actionable next steps (short term):
- Add systemd drop-in to require cloud-final.service for kubelet on GKE custom image (patch in node image bake).
- Add udevadm settle in cloud-init before starting kubelet.
- Throttle concurrent PVC attach operations in CSI controller as a temporary mitigation.
- Add a small startup probe for kube-proxy / cni pods to prevent scheduling too early.

Longer term / engineering:
- Improve kubelet to better retry mount attach for longer windows when node is freshly booted and devices appear shortly after (file issue upstream).
- Provide orchestration signal: provisioning service emits a ready-to-schedule marker that kubelet honors before reporting Ready. Discuss in infra design review.

Helpful links and references I used while debugging:
- kubelet mount volume errors: https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/command-line-tools-reference/kubelet/
- CSI attach/mount patterns: https://kubernetes-csi.github.io/
- systemd ordering docs: https://www.freedesktop.org/wiki/Software/systemd/

Random breadcrumbs to follow up on (tickets / TODOs):
- Re-run repro with debug logging enabled for kubelet + csi plugin (capture full journal) -> attach to JIRA-INFRA-3421.
- Try a variant without cloud-init modifications but with artificially delayed containerd to see if containerd vs udev order matters.
- Coordinate with platform-images team to bake a node image that adjusts kubelet unit ordering.

If you pick this up: start by SSHing to a recent node that flapped and run journalctl -u kubelet -b -1 to see previous boot logs. I left some of the raw journal extracts in the incident ticket.

End of scratchpad.

-- Ava M.
